newsitem.title: DUBAI: HORSE RACING-DUBAI RACE TRACK STILL CLOSED AFTER RAIN.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-DUBAI RACE TRACK STILL CLOSED AFTER RAIN.

text.p: Dubai's sand race track remained sealed off on Thursday, two days after a downpour left large tracts of desert under water and two days before the world's richest horse race.

Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe winner Helissio, Europe's best hope in the international field of 13 thoroughbreds chasing a gold cup and $2.4 million first prize, was taken to American trainer Kiaran McLaughlin's nearby stables.
There he breezed over 1,000 metres of dirt training track in a time of 1:01 minutes.
Last year's inaugural running of the 2,000 metre (mile and a quarter) Dubai World Cup was won by American wonder horse Cigar in a time of 2:03.84 minutes.
Saturday night's race for a total $4 million prize-money is due to be run on the sand track at Dubai's floodlit Nad al-Sheba course.

Siphon and Sandpit, the two Brazilian-bred and owned first and second favourites trained by Richard Mandella in California, did not go out on Thursday after working well on Wednesday, race officials said.
They said the track remained closed so that it could continue to dry out from Tuesday night's downpour, which gave much of Dubai's desert landscape a glassy appearance.
"The track will be fine if there is no more rain and if it doesn't rain on the night," said McLaughlin, trainer of Key of Luck who has drawn on the outside of the field at 13th place from the rail.
McLaughlin professed himself happy to be drawn wide. "I didn't want to be drawn on the inner close to Siphon," he said.
Nad al-Sheba's turf course was open on Thursday and first out was the Gai Waterhouse-trained Australian Juggler partnered by big race jockey Glen Boss.

Some other contenders were transported to nearby dirt tracks. World Cup host Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid's Flemensfirth went to Jebel Ali racecourse and his other entry, Breeders Cup and Japan Cup winner Singspiel, travelled to Al Quoz training track.
